**7B.9 Research Note: Shehbaz Sharif in 2024**

Overall read: **mixed, leaning negative**. I found some real anti-patronage signals in economic staffing and welfare delivery, but the year is more strongly marked by family/political influence in appointments and by repeated state control over media, protest, and scrutiny.

**Positive / mitigating evidence**
- `Pakistan’s largest parties strike deal on coalition government` — Reuters via ThePrint, `2024-02-21`, https://theprint.in/world/pakistans-largest-parties-strike-deal-on-coalition-government-says-ex-foreign-minister/1973194/  
  Claim: Sharif returned through coalition bargaining after a hung parliament, which is a weak positive for procedural rather than purely personalist power transfer.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `Pakistan PM to choose banker Aurangzeb as finance minister, sources say` — Reuters via ThePrint, `2024-03-11`, https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-to-choose-banker-aurangzeb-as-finance-minister-sources-say/1996592/  
  Claim: Sharif selected a career banker rather than a party loyalist for finance, which is one of the clearest anti-patronage staffing signals in 2024.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `PM forms new Economic Advisory Council without Dar, Aurangzeb` — The News, `2024-05-19`, https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/1190715-pm-forms-new-economic-advisory-council-without-dar-aurangzeb  
  Claim: Sharif created a technocratic advisory council with economists and business figures, showing some willingness to bring expertise into policy rather than rely only on partisan networks.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `PM Shehbaz directs full digitalization of social welfare payments under BISP` — APP, `2024-03-18`, https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-directs-full-digitalization-of-social-welfare-payments-under-bisp/  
  Claim: Moving BISP payments onto digital wallets was framed as reducing leakage, delay, and discretion, which is concrete anti-clientelism delivery reform.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `BISP says aid goes to poor and deserving people regardless of political affiliation` — Benazir Income Support Programme, `2024-05-23`, https://www.bisp.gov.pk/NewsDetail/MjU0NDA1ZTItM2NiOC00NGE4LWJmNzctNGFiZTY4ZDFiZGFj  
  Claim: The program publicly described its aid as nonpartisan and transparent, which supports a non-clientelist welfare model, though this is institutional self-description rather than independent verification.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `Pakistan renegotiating power deals to cut costs, minister says` — Reuters via Dawn, `2024-10-10`, https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1864298  
  Claim: Renegotiating costly power contracts to lower tariffs and save public money is a plausible anti-rent, anti-favoritism move in procurement-adjacent policy.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `Pakistan to investigate army's meddling in judiciary, law minister says` — Reuters via Al Jazeera, `2024-03-28`, https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/3/28/pakistan-to-investigate-armys-meddling-in-judiciary-law-minister-says  
  Claim: The government announced an inquiry commission after judges alleged intimidation, which is a limited positive for not burying a politically sensitive abuse claim.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `PM orders action over ‘ineffective’ track, trace system` — Dawn, `2024-05-08`, https://www.dawn.com/news/1832117  
  Claim: Sharif ordered action after an internal report found the FBR track-and-trace system ineffective, which is evidence of at least some corrective behavior rather than silent protection of a failing setup.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

**Negative evidence**
- `Shehbaz takes U-turn on ‘military’s darling’ claim` — Dawn, `2024-02-01`, https://www.dawn.com/news/1810266/shehbaz-takes-u-turn-on-militarys-darling-claim  
  Claim: Sharif publicly reversed an earlier boast when challenged, which is direct rhetorical evidence of opportunistic repositioning.  
  IDs: `7B.9`, `7B.8`

- `Nawaz busy selecting cabinet as Khawaja Asif sees PPP-N govt` — Dawn, `2024-02-19`, https://www.dawn.com/news/1815365/nawaz-busy-selecting-cabinet-as-khawaja-asif-sees-ppp-n-govt  
  Claim: Reporting that Nawaz Sharif was heavily involved in cabinet selection is indirect but meaningful evidence of family influence over appointments.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `The cabinet still leaned heavily on old political hands` — Dawn, `2024-03-01`, https://www.dawn.com/news/1821157  
  Claim: The cabinet composition remained dominated by established political figures, which weakens any claim of a clean meritocratic or anti-nepotistic break.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `Sharif retained direct control over a key economic coordination body` — Dawn, `2024-06-15`, https://www.dawn.com/news/1839967  
  Claim: Sharif kept hands-on control over ECNEC instead of fully delegating to the technocrat finance minister, which suggests personalized executive management still dominated.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `Social media platform X blocked in Pakistan over national security, ministry says` — Reuters via Investing.com, `2024-04-17`, https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313  
  Claim: The state blocked X on national-security grounds during a politically sensitive period, restricting criticism, reporting, and monitoring.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `Pakistan widening crackdown on dissent` — Human Rights Watch, `2024-01-11`, https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent  
  Claim: HRW said the government clamped down on media, opposition, and NGOs, and that pressure and weak safeguards deepened self-censorship.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `Pakistan the new peaceful assembly and public order act threatens the right to protest` — Amnesty International, `2024-09-09`, https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/  
  Claim: Amnesty said the government rushed through a law that criminalized peaceful assembly and expanded restriction powers, which fits transactional control over dissent rather than neutral enforcement.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `Pakistan’s government curbs judiciary’s power after alleged harassment of MPs` — The Guardian, `2024-10-21`, https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps  
  Claim: Critics said the 26th Amendment weakened judicial independence and passed amid intimidation allegations, which is strong evidence against preserving neutral oversight.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

- `U.S. Department of State human-rights report on Pakistan` — U.S. Department of State via ecoi.net, `2024`, https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128431.html  
  Claim: The report says PEMRA, PTA, network access, government advertising, and FIA notices were used to pressure media and suppress threatening information, which is strong evidence of informational favoritism and state-backed concealment.  
  IDs: `7B.9`

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence of a Sharif-linked pardon/clemency decision.
- I also did not find a clean, direct 2024 procurement scandal attributable to Sharif personally; the closest relevant evidence was the power-contract renegotiation, which reads more like cost repair than favoritism.
- The strongest anti-nepotism evidence is mostly indirect: cabinet composition, family involvement in selection, and continued PM-centered control. The strongest anti-clientelism evidence is stronger on welfare delivery than on appointments.
